message: AMI Block Public Access is enabled in us-east-2.
status_detail: AMI Block Public Access is enabled in us-east-2.

analytic.name: AMI block public access is enabled at the account level

finding_info.desc: AMI block public access configuration is assessed to see whether public sharing of AMIs is blocked in the account and Region. When enabled (`block-new-sharing`), no AMI in the Region can be made public regardless of individual image permissions.
finding_info.title: AMI block public access is enabled at the account level
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable AMI block public access (`block-new-sharing`) in every active Region. Apply guardrails (SCPs) to prevent it from being disabled, and review any AMIs that are currently shared publicly.

risk_details: Without blocking public access, AMIs could be accidentally or maliciously shared publicly, exposing baked-in secrets, source code, and infrastructure details to unauthorized actors.

message: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.
status_detail: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.

analytic.name: EBS default encryption is enabled

finding_info.desc: **EBS** uses `encryption by default` at the account and region level, ensuring new volumes, snapshots, and AMI-backed volumes are automatically encrypted with a chosen **KMS key**
finding_info.title: EBS default encryption is enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable `EBS encryption by default` in every region and select a **customer-managed KMS key**. Apply **least privilege** to key use, rotate keys, and monitor access. Enforce encrypted volume creation with organizational guardrails and secure templates as **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Without `encryption by default`, data on new **EBS volumes** and **snapshots** may be stored in plaintext. A compromised account or mis-shared snapshot can expose disk contents, enabling data exfiltration, offline analysis, and loss of **confidentiality**.

message: Public access is not blocked for EBS Snapshots.
status_detail: Public access is not blocked for EBS Snapshots.

analytic.name: All EBS snapshots have public access blocked

finding_info.desc: **EBS snapshots** account/Region configuration for **Block Public Access** is assessed to see whether public sharing is fully blocked (`block-all-sharing`) versus only new sharing (`block-new-sharing`) or unblocked. The state indicates if any snapshot can be publicly shared.
finding_info.title: All EBS snapshots have public access blocked
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Set **Block Public Access** for EBS snapshots to `block-all-sharing` in all active Regions.

Apply **least privilege** and guardrails (SCPs) to prevent changes. Regularly inventory snapshots, remove public sharing, and use segregated accounts with strict reviews for any necessary external sharing.

risk_details:
Without `block-all-sharing`, previously public snapshots can remain accessible, exposing raw disk data.

Impacts:
- Loss of **confidentiality** (PII, keys, configs)
- Unauthorized cloning enabling **lateral movement**
- Cross-account copies create **irreversible data leakage**

message: EBS Snapshot vol-02fad3ea9b47bf4f7 is encrypted.
status_detail: EBS Snapshot vol-02fad3ea9b47bf4f7 is encrypted.

analytic.name: EBS volume is encrypted

finding_info.desc:
**EBS volumes** are assessed for **encryption at rest** using **AWS KMS**.

The finding identifies volumes whose `encrypted` state is disabled, meaning data is stored unencrypted on block storage.
finding_info.title: EBS volume is encrypted
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Encrypt all EBS volumes and enable `encryption by default` for new volumes and snapshot copies.

Apply **least privilege** to KMS keys, restrict snapshot sharing, and enforce **defense in depth** with policies and templates that prevent creation of unencrypted storage.

risk_details:
Unencrypted volumes or snapshots can be copied, shared, or recovered and reveal raw data, undermining **confidentiality**.

Adversaries with host or account access can read disks offline, harvest secrets, or alter system images, affecting **integrity** and enabling **lateral movement**.

message: EBS Volume vol-02fad3ea9b47bf4f7 is not protected by a backup plan.
status_detail: EBS Volume vol-02fad3ea9b47bf4f7 is not protected by a backup plan.

analytic.name: EBS volume is protected by a backup plan

finding_info.desc: **EBS volumes** are evaluated for coverage by an **AWS Backup plan**, whether explicitly targeted or included via broad resource selection, confirming scheduled, policy-driven backups exist for the volume.
finding_info.title: EBS volume is protected by a backup plan
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc: Include all critical EBS volumes in standardized **AWS Backup** plans aligned to your `RPO`/`RTO`. Use tags for automatic assignment, enable cross-Region/account copies, apply **Vault Lock** for WORM retention, encrypt with KMS, enforce least-privilege access, and regularly test restores to verify integrity.

risk_details: Absent backup coverage, volumes face **data loss**, weakened **integrity**, and reduced **availability**. Deletion or corruption-whether accidental or malicious-can leave no recovery path, causing prolonged outages, failed point-in-time restoration, unmet retention needs, and harder incident response.

message: Snapshots not found for the EBS volume vol-02fad3ea9b47bf4f7.
status_detail: Snapshots not found for the EBS volume vol-02fad3ea9b47bf4f7.

analytic.name: EBS volume has at least one snapshot

finding_info.desc: **EBS volumes** are evaluated for the existence of at least one associated **snapshot**, identifying volumes without any point-in-time backup available.
finding_info.title: EBS volume has at least one snapshot
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Establish automated, policy-based **EBS snapshot** coverage for all volumes aligned to business `RPO/RTO`.
- Schedule regular snapshots with retention controls
- Encrypt snapshots and enforce **least privilege** access
- Replicate to another Region/account for DR
- Periodically test restores and document procedures

risk_details: Missing **EBS snapshots** removes point-in-time recovery. Accidental deletion, corruption, or ransomware can cause **irrecoverable data loss** and prolonged **service outages**, degrading data **integrity** and **availability** and complicating recovery and forensics.

message: IMDSv2 is not enabled by default for EC2 instances.
status_detail: IMDSv2 is not enabled by default for EC2 instances.

analytic.name: IMDSv2 is required by default for EC2 instances at the account level

finding_info.desc: **EC2 account IMDS defaults** with `http_tokens`=`required` ensure new instances in the Region use **IMDSv2** by default and disable IMDSv1. *Existing instances keep their current setting.*
finding_info.title: IMDSv2 is required by default for EC2 instances at the account level
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc: Enforce **IMDSv2** at the account level in every Region by setting `http_tokens` to `required`. Add guardrails with **SCP/IAM conditions**. Standardize AMIs and launch templates to require tokens, validate workload compatibility, and apply **least privilege** to instance roles for defense in depth. *For containers*, prefer hop limit `2`.

risk_details: Without a default of **IMDSv2**, new instances may enable **IMDSv1**, exposing metadata via simple HTTP. SSRF or proxy misconfigs can steal **temporary IAM credentials**, enabling data exfiltration (confidentiality), unauthorized API changes (integrity), and lateral movement that can disrupt services (availability).

message: EC2 Instance i-0c769bc09bb9140ea does not have detailed monitoring enabled.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0c769bc09bb9140ea does not have detailed monitoring enabled.

analytic.name: EC2 instance has detailed monitoring enabled

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** are assessed for **CloudWatch detailed monitoring**, indicating whether 1-minute metrics collection is enabled.

Instances lacking this setting provide only 5-minute metrics.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance has detailed monitoring enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Enable **detailed monitoring** to collect `1-minute` metrics on critical instances. Use **defense in depth**: baseline normal behavior, create alerts for anomalies, and correlate metrics with logs and traces. Review dashboards regularly. *If costs matter*, prioritize production, internet-facing, and autoscaling fleets.

risk_details:
Without 1-minute metrics, visibility drops, delaying detection of:
- Sudden CPU/network/disk spikes affecting **availability**
- **Malicious workloads** (crypto-mining, brute force)
- **Data exfiltration** patterns
Slower detection expands blast radius, raising incident impact and response cost.

message: EC2 Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 has IMDSv2 enabled and required.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 has IMDSv2 enabled and required.

analytic.name: EC2 instance requires IMDSv2 or has the instance metadata service disabled

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for **IMDSv2 enforcement**: metadata endpoint enabled with `http_tokens: required`, or metadata service fully disabled (`http_endpoint: disabled`).
finding_info.title: EC2 instance requires IMDSv2 or has the instance metadata service disabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc:
Apply defense in depth:
- Require **IMDSv2** tokens on all instances (`http_tokens: required`)
- Disable metadata where not needed (`http_endpoint: disabled`)
- Minimize hop limit to `1` when feasible
- Update SDKs/apps for IMDSv2
- Restrict instance profile permissions (least privilege)
- Block metadata access from untrusted workloads

risk_details: Permitting **IMDSv1** or optional tokens lets SSRF or compromised workloads retrieve **temporary IAM credentials**, impacting confidentiality and integrity. Stolen role creds can drive **privilege escalation**, unauthorized data access, and lateral movement across AWS resources.

message: EC2 Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 at IP 3.135.221.119 is internet-facing with Instance Profile arn:aws:iam::123456789012:instance-profile/datalake-etl-role.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 at IP 3.135.221.119 is internet-facing with Instance Profile arn:aws:iam::123456789012:instance-profile/datalake-etl-role.

analytic.name: EC2 instance is not internet-facing with an instance profile attached

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** with a public IP address and an attached **instance profile** (IAM role) are identified.

Instances lacking public exposure or without an instance profile are excluded.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is not internet-facing with an instance profile attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
TTPs/Initial Access
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc: Avoid direct Internet exposure. Place workloads behind an **Application Load Balancer** and protect HTTP apps with **WAF**. Remove public IPs or restrict ingress to trusted sources. Apply **least privilege** to instance profiles and enforce **IMDSv2**. Use **bastion hosts** or **Session Manager** for admin access.

risk_details: Publicly reachable instances with **IAM role credentials** expand the blast radius. Remote exploits or misconfigurations can steal credentials via the **instance metadata service**, enabling unauthorized API calls, data exfiltration, and lateral movement, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

message: Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 has SSH exposed to 0.0.0.0/0 on public IP address 3.135.221.119 in public subnet subnet-024f58fc9f76ab09c.
status_detail: Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 has SSH exposed to 0.0.0.0/0 on public IP address 3.135.221.119 in public subnet subnet-024f58fc9f76ab09c.

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 22 (SSH)

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** with **SSH (TCP 22)** exposed to the Internet via security group inbound rules allowing `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`.

Exposure is qualified using the instance's public IP status and subnet reachability.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 22 (SSH)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access/External Remote Services

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** on SSH:
- Restrict ingress to trusted IPs; avoid `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`
- Prefer **Session Manager** or a hardened **bastion** behind VPN
- Use **key-based auth**; disable passwords
- Add **defense in depth** with network controls and monitor access logs

risk_details: **Internet-exposed SSH** invites **brute force** and **credential stuffing**. A successful sign-in grants **remote shell**, enabling data exfiltration, tampering of workloads, and **lateral movement** within the VPC, degrading confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

message: EC2 Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 has a Public IP: 3.135.221.119 (ec2-3-135-221-119.us-east-2.compute.amazonaws.com).
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-0b861a4f57ea57684 has a Public IP: 3.135.221.119 (ec2-3-135-221-119.us-east-2.compute.amazonaws.com).

analytic.name: EC2 instance does not have a public IP address

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are assessed for the presence of a **public IPv4 address** and public DNS. A public IP indicates the instance is directly reachable from the Internet; no public IP implies access only through private networking paths such as load balancers, gateways, or proxies.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance does not have a public IP address
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc: Avoid assigning public IPs unless strictly required. Place workloads in private subnets and expose only via **load balancers** with **WAF**; use **bastions** or **Session Manager** for administration. Enforce **least privilege** security groups, prefer **private endpoints**, and route egress via **NAT** for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Publicly addressed instances are Internet-scannable, enabling direct probing and brute-force of exposed services and management ports. This increases risks of unauthorized access, remote code execution, and data exfiltration (**confidentiality, integrity**), and allows direct DDoS targeting, degrading **availability**.

message: Network ACL acl-0befc13ff76c6e230 has every port open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-0befc13ff76c6e230 has every port open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to any port

finding_info.desc: **VPC network ACLs** with **inbound entries** that permit traffic from `0.0.0.0/0` to any port (any protocol) are identified at the subnet boundary.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to any port
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Adopt a **deny-by-default** NACL posture: block `0.0.0.0/0` and allow only required ports from trusted CIDRs. Apply **least privilege** using security groups for fine-grained access, with NACLs as coarse stateless filters. Review and prune rules regularly, and employ **defense in depth** with monitoring and alerting.

risk_details: Allowing Internet-wide ingress at the subnet layer enables broad port scanning and unsolicited connections. Attackers can probe and exploit exposed services, risking data disclosure and tampering (confidentiality, integrity) and causing outages via floods or brute-force (availability). Any security group lapse then lacks a compensating control.

message: Network ACL acl-0befc13ff76c6e230 has SSH port 22 open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-0befc13ff76c6e230 has SSH port 22 open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 22 (SSH)

finding_info.desc: **VPC network ACLs** are evaluated for inbound rules that permit `0.0.0.0/0` to access **SSH** on `TCP 22` at the subnet boundary.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 22 (SSH)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** at the subnet layer:
- Do not allow `0.0.0.0/0` to `TCP 22`
- Restrict SSH to trusted sources, or avoid direct SSH via **Session Manager** or a bastion behind **VPN**

Pair tight **security groups** with periodic rule reviews and change control to maintain **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
An ACL allowing Internet-wide SSH erodes **defense in depth**. Systems reachable on `TCP 22` face **brute-force**, credential stuffing, reconnaissance, and SSH exploit attempts.

Changes to routes or security groups can create direct exposure, enabling unauthorized access and **lateral movement**, undermining **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

message: Network ACL acl-0befc13ff76c6e230 has Microsoft RDP port 3389 open to the Internet.
status_detail: Network ACL acl-0befc13ff76c6e230 has Microsoft RDP port 3389 open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 3389 (RDP)

finding_info.desc:
**VPC network ACLs** with inbound rules allowing **RDP** on `TCP 3389` from `0.0.0.0/0` are identified.

Assessment focuses on subnet-level ACL entries that permit this traffic.
finding_info.title: Network ACL does not allow ingress from the Internet to TCP port 3389 (RDP)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc:
Enforce **least privilege**: do not allow `TCP 3389` from `0.0.0.0/0` in network ACLs.

- Restrict RDP to specific admin IP ranges
- Prefer **bastion hosts** or **Session Manager** over direct RDP
- Use private subnets and layer controls for **defense in depth**

risk_details: Internet-exposed **RDP** enables **password spraying**, brute force, and exploitation of RDP flaws to gain remote control. Allowing it at the subnet layer weakens **defense in depth**-a misconfigured security group or route can expose instances-leading to data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and ransomware, impacting confidentiality and integrity.

status_detail: Security group datalake-etl-sg (sg-0586c5b38f77d2611) has at least one port open to the Internet but its network interface type (interface) is not allowed.

analytic.name: Security group has no 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 ingress to any port, or is attached only to allowed interface types or instance owners

finding_info.desc: **EC2 security groups** with **internet-sourced ingress** from `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` to any port, and their attachments, are evaluated. Groups linked to network interfaces or instance owners outside an approved list for public exposure are identified.
finding_info.title: Security group has no 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 ingress to any port, or is attached only to allowed interface types or instance owners
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access

remediation.desc: Apply **least privilege**: restrict ingress to required ports and trusted sources; avoid `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` except for managed public endpoints. Place workloads behind **load balancers**, **API gateways**, or **WAFs**; use **private networking**. Allow public rules only on approved interface types.

risk_details: Open ingress to any port on non-approved interfaces enables external scanning, brute force, and exploitation of unintended services. This threatens **confidentiality** (unauthorized access), **integrity** (tampering), and **availability** (DoS), and facilitates **lateral movement**.

message: Security group datalake-etl-sg (sg-0586c5b38f77d2611) has SSH port 22 open to the Internet.
status_detail: Security group datalake-etl-sg (sg-0586c5b38f77d2611) has SSH port 22 open to the Internet.

analytic.name: Security group does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to TCP port 22 (SSH)

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 security groups** are assessed for **inbound SSH exposure** by locating ingress rules that allow `TCP 22` from the Internet (`0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`).

Only groups in use are considered; sets already flagged for all-port exposure are not repeated.
finding_info.title: Security group does not allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to TCP port 22 (SSH)
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Initial Access/Unauthorized Access

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** to SSH:
- Disallow `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`; allow only trusted IPs or VPN ranges
- Prefer **private access** via bastion hosts or AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
- Enforce **key-based auth**, disable passwords, rotate keys
- Add **network segmentation** and monitoring for **defense in depth**

risk_details: Exposed **SSH** invites Internet-scale **brute force** and **credential stuffing**. A successful login grants **remote shell**, enabling data theft (confidentiality), code or config tampering (integrity), and cryptomining or service disruption (availability), plus **lateral movement** within the environment.

message: Default Security Group (sg-028d6b51a3696cfdb) rules allow traffic.
status_detail: Default Security Group (sg-028d6b51a3696cfdb) rules allow traffic.

analytic.name: VPC default security group has no inbound or outbound rules

finding_info.desc: **Default VPC security group** should have **no inbound or outbound rules**. This evaluates whether the group allows any traffic-ingress, egress, or self-referencing-instead of remaining empty.
finding_info.title: VPC default security group has no inbound or outbound rules
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enforce **least privilege**: keep the default group empty by removing all ingress and egress rules. Use dedicated security groups per workload with explicit sources, destinations, and ports. Regularly review for broad CIDRs like `0.0.0.0/0` and apply **defense in depth** via automation and policy guardrails.

risk_details: Permissive rules in the **default security group** mean instances that inherit it can communicate widely. This enables **lateral movement**, **port scanning**, and **data exfiltration**; unrestricted egress aids **C2**. Confidentiality and integrity are reduced, and the blast radius of a compromise grows.

message: AWS policy AdministratorAccess is attached and allows '*:*' administrative privileges.
status_detail: AWS policy AdministratorAccess is attached and allows '*:*' administrative privileges.

analytic.name: Attached AWS-managed IAM policy does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges

finding_info.desc: **IAM AWS-managed policies** attached to identities are inspected for statements that allow `Action:'*'` on `Resource:'*'`-i.e., full administrative `*:*` permissions
finding_info.title: Attached AWS-managed IAM policy does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege**: avoid attaching AWS-managed policies that grant `*:*`.
- Use **customer-managed, scoped policies** per role
- Enforce **separation of duties** and **permissions boundaries**
- Prefer **temporary, time-bound elevation** for emergencies with MFA
- Regularly review access and use conditions to constrain context

risk_details:
**Unrestricted `*:*` access** enables any action on any resource, risking:
- Data exfiltration (**confidentiality**)
- Unauthorized changes and policy tampering (**integrity**)
- Service deletion or shutdown (**availability**)
Attackers can disable logging, create backdoor principals, and expand lateral movement.

analytic.name: IAM inline policy does not allow privilege escalation

finding_info.desc: **IAM inline policies** are evaluated for permission combinations that enable **privilege escalation**, such as `sts:AssumeRole`, `iam:PassRole`, attaching/editing policies, or broad wildcards. The result highlights inline policies that allow a principal to obtain higher effective access.
finding_info.title: IAM inline policy does not allow privilege escalation
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** and remove escalation paths:
- Avoid wildcards and sensitive actions like `sts:AssumeRole`, `iam:PassRole`, or policy modification without tight scope
- Restrict by resource and `Condition`
- Prefer managed, versioned policies; use permissions boundaries/SCPs
- Require reviews and MFA for admins

risk_details:
Excessive inline policy permissions let identities escalate to admin, compromising CIA:
- Confidentiality: read secrets and data
- Integrity: alter policies, code, and configs
- Availability: delete or stop resources, disable logging
Attackers can persist by creating keys/users or assuming powerful roles.

message: Inline policy datalake-etl-inline attached to role datalake-etl-role allows '*:*' administrative privileges.
status_detail: Inline policy datalake-etl-inline attached to role datalake-etl-role allows '*:*' administrative privileges.

analytic.name: Inline IAM policy does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges

finding_info.desc: **IAM inline policies** on identities are evaluated for statements allowing `Action:"*"` on `Resource:"*"`, which indicates **unrestricted administrative access**.
finding_info.title: Inline IAM policy does not allow '*:*' administrative privileges
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc: Remove `Action:"*"` with `Resource:"*"` from inline policies. Apply **least privilege** with granular actions scoped to specific resources and conditions. Prefer versioned customer-managed policies over broad inline ones, enforce **separation of duties**, and use **permissions boundaries** or guardrails to prevent accidental admin grants.

risk_details: Granting `*:*` to an identity collapses **least privilege**, enabling total control over AWS. A compromised principal can exfiltrate data (**confidentiality**), alter configs or disable logging (**integrity**), and delete resources or keys (**availability**), enabling rapid **lateral movement** and persistent takeover.

message: Inline policy datalake-etl-inline attached to role datalake-etl-role allows 'cloudtrail:*' privileges to all resources.
status_detail: Inline policy datalake-etl-inline attached to role datalake-etl-role allows 'cloudtrail:*' privileges to all resources.

analytic.name: Inline IAM policy does not allow 'cloudtrail:*' privileges

finding_info.desc:
**IAM inline policies** are evaluated for statements that grant **full CloudTrail permissions** (`cloudtrail:*`) to all resources.

The finding flags identity policies that provide unrestricted control over CloudTrail operations.
finding_info.title: Inline IAM policy does not allow 'cloudtrail:*' privileges
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Defense Evasion

remediation.desc: Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties**: avoid `cloudtrail:*`; grant only specific actions needed (prefer read-only where possible). Add guardrails or boundaries to block destructive actions. Use managed, centrally governed policies and periodically right-size permissions based on usage.

risk_details: Full CloudTrail access allows stopping trails, modifying configurations, or deleting audit data, compromising log **integrity** and **availability**. It also exposes event data, impacting **confidentiality**. Adversaries could hide activity, evade detection, and obstruct investigations.

message: Inline policy datalake-etl-inline attached to role datalake-etl-role allows 'kms:*' privileges.
status_detail: Inline policy datalake-etl-inline attached to role datalake-etl-role allows 'kms:*' privileges.

analytic.name: Inline IAM policy does not allow kms:* privileges

finding_info.desc: **IAM inline policies** are analyzed to identify statements that grant **unrestricted AWS KMS access** via the wildcard action `kms:*`.
finding_info.title: Inline IAM policy does not allow kms:* privileges
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Privilege Escalation
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Replace `kms:*` with **least-privilege**, action-scoped permissions limited to required operations and specific key ARNs. Enforce **separation of duties** for key admins vs users. Prefer **managed policies** over inline and apply guardrails (permissions boundaries/SCPs). Add conditions to constrain service, region, and encryption context.

risk_details:
Granting `kms:*` enables decryption of protected data, modification of key policies and grants, and disabling or deleting keys.

Impacts:
- **Confidentiality** via unauthorized decryption
- **Integrity** through key/grant tampering
- **Availability** if keys are disabled or deleted, breaking encrypted workloads

This action controls the ability to subscribe to AWS Marketplace products, including **Amazon Bedrock foundation models**, and should be scoped to specific product ARNs to enforce least privilege.
finding_info.title: Inline IAM policy does not allow 'aws-marketplace:Subscribe' on all resources
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Replace `Resource: "*"` with specific, approved AWS Marketplace product ARNs. Prefer managed policies over inline and apply the principle of least privilege to `aws-marketplace:Subscribe` permissions to prevent unauthorized subscriptions to costly Bedrock models and other Marketplace products.

risk_details: Granting `aws-marketplace:Subscribe` on all resources via inline policies allows subscribing to any Marketplace product, including expensive Bedrock foundation models, leading to uncontrolled costs, shadow AI usage, and compliance violations.

status_detail: Password expiration is not set.

analytic.name: IAM account password policy enforces password expiration within 90 days or less

finding_info.desc: **IAM account password policy** sets a **password expiration period** for IAM user console logins; configuration is aligned when rotation is enabled and set to `<= 90` days.
finding_info.title: IAM account password policy enforces password expiration within 90 days or less
types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enforce **password rotation** at `<= 90` days and **prevent reuse**. Pair with **MFA**, strong length/complexity, and prefer **federation/SSO** to reduce static passwords. Apply **least privilege**, monitor sign-ins, and remove inactive console passwords to limit exposure.

risk_details: Without rotation, stale passwords persist, enabling **credential stuffing**, **brute force**, and **password reuse** attacks. A compromised IAM user can retain console access, enabling **data exfiltration**, privilege escalation, and loss of **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

message: IAM password policy does not require at least one lowercase letter.
status_detail: IAM password policy does not require at least one lowercase letter.

analytic.name: IAM password policy requires at least one lowercase letter

finding_info.desc: **IAM password policy** requires at least one **lowercase** character in user passwords via the `Require lowercase` setting
finding_info.title: IAM password policy requires at least one lowercase letter
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Adopt a strong password policy that:
- Enables `Require at least one lowercase letter` plus uppercase, number, and symbol
- Sets sufficient length and blocks reuse
- Requires **MFA** for all users
- Applies **least privilege** to limit blast radius

risk_details: Without a lowercase requirement, passwords have reduced entropy, making **brute force** and **password spraying** more effective. Compromised IAM users can enable unauthorized access and changes, risking **confidentiality**, **integrity**, and **availability** of AWS resources.

types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Set the **minimum password length** to `>= 14` (prefer `16+`).
- Require mixed character types and prevent reuse
- Enforce **MFA** for all console users
- Prefer SSO over local IAM users
- Apply least privilege and monitor authentication events

risk_details: Low minimum length reduces entropy, easing **brute force** and **credential stuffing**. Compromised IAM users enable console access, unauthorized changes, and lateral movement, leading to data exposure (confidentiality) and tampering (integrity).

remediation.desc: Enforce the password policy option to `require at least one number`. Combine with strong length, mixed case, and symbols, and prevent reuse. Enable **MFA** for all users and prefer **federated access** to limit static credentials, supporting **defense in depth** against guessing attacks.

risk_details: Passwords without numbers have lower entropy, making **brute-force** and **credential-stuffing** more effective. A compromised IAM user can gain console access, enabling data exposure (**confidentiality**), configuration changes (**integrity**), and resource abuse or deletion (**availability**).

status_detail: IAM password policy reuse prevention is less than 24 or not set.

analytic.name: IAM password policy prevents reuse of the last 24 passwords

finding_info.desc: **IAM account password policy** uses **password reuse prevention** set to `24` remembered passwords (maximum history) for IAM users
finding_info.title: IAM password policy prevents reuse of the last 24 passwords
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Set the password policy to remember `24` previous passwords to block reuse. Combine with **MFA**, strong length and complexity, and avoid rotation practices that encourage predictable patterns. Apply **least privilege** and monitor authentication events as part of **defense in depth**.

risk_details: If fewer than `24` passwords are remembered, users can cycle back to recent secrets, undermining rotation. Attackers with previously exposed passwords can regain console access after a change, reducing **confidentiality** and **integrity** and increasing success of credential-stuffing with known credentials.

Apply **MFA** for all human users and uphold **least privilege** to limit impact. *Consider periodic rotation based on risk.*

risk_details: Missing a **symbol requirement** lowers password entropy, increasing success of **brute force** and **credential stuffing** against console logins. A compromised IAM user can gain unauthorized access and modify resources, threatening **confidentiality** and **integrity** across the account.

risk_details: Without an uppercase requirement, passwords have lower entropy, enabling **brute force**, **credential stuffing**, and **offline cracking**. status_detail: IAM Role AccountFullAccessRole has Bedrock permissions but has never used them.

unmapped.notes: The staleness threshold is configurable via the `max_unused_bedrock_access_days` audit config key (default: 60 days).

analytic.name: Regular Bedrock access ensures IAM roles retain only actively used permissions

finding_info.desc:
IAM roles granted **Bedrock** permissions are evaluated for recent service usage.

Roles whose last Bedrock access exceeds the configured threshold (default **60 days**) or that have **never** accessed Bedrock are flagged, indicating stale permissions that should be reviewed.
finding_info.title: Regular Bedrock access ensures IAM roles retain only actively used permissions
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Apply the **principle of least privilege** by regularly reviewing IAM Access Advisor data and revoking Bedrock permissions that are no longer actively used.

Establish a periodic access review process and automate alerts for stale permissions to maintain a minimal attack surface.

risk_details:
Stale Bedrock permissions widen the **blast radius** of a credential compromise.

An attacker who assumes a role with unused Bedrock permissions can invoke foundation models, exfiltrate data through model responses, or incur significant costs — all without triggering expected usage patterns.

message: IAM Service Role AccountFullAccessRole does not prevent against a cross-service confused deputy attack.
status_detail: IAM Service Role AccountFullAccessRole does not prevent against a cross-service confused deputy attack.

analytic.name: IAM service role prevents cross-service confused deputy attack

finding_info.desc: **IAM service role** trust policies restrict **AWS service principals** to expected sources using global condition keys like `aws:SourceArn` or `aws:SourceAccount`, avoiding overly broad `sts:AssumeRole` trust relationships.
finding_info.title: IAM service role prevents cross-service confused deputy attack
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
TTPs/Privilege Escalation

remediation.desc: Constrain service-role trust to expected callers using `aws:SourceArn`/`aws:SourceAccount` to bind service principals to specific resources or accounts. If unsupported, apply equivalent limits in resource-based policies or org-level controls. Apply **least privilege** and review trust relationships regularly.

risk_details:
Unrestricted service-principal trust lets outsiders trigger a **cross-service confused deputy**, causing unintended `sts:AssumeRole`.
This can enable data exfiltration, unauthorized changes, and lateral movement, impacting **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

status_detail: Root credentials management is not enabled.

analytic.name: AWS Organization has centralized root credentials management enabled

finding_info.desc:
**AWS Organizations** uses **centralized root credentials management** to control root user credentials across member accounts.

This finding evaluates whether the organization has enabled the `RootCredentialsManagement` feature to centrally govern presence and recovery of root passwords, access keys, signing certificates, and MFA.
finding_info.title: AWS Organization has centralized root credentials management enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc:
Enable centralized root access with **root credentials management** and assign a **delegated administrator**.

Apply **least privilege** and **separation of duties** by deleting long-term root credentials in members, limiting privileged tasks to short-lived sessions, enforcing **MFA**, and auditing root-related activity for **defense in depth**.

risk_details:
Without central control, member accounts can retain or recover long-term root credentials, weakening **confidentiality** and **integrity**.

Threats include:
- Account takeover via root email recovery
- Persistent access through root keys
- Unfixable lockouts from misconfigured policies
- Bypass of **separation of duties**

Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Establish a dedicated **audit role** and attach the AWS managed `SecurityAudit` policy. Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties**: restrict who can assume it, require **MFA**, monitor usage, and avoid write permissions. Prefer **federated access** and regularly review and rotate access.

risk_details: Without a dedicated **read-only audit role**, security teams lack safe visibility into configs and logs, enabling **undetected misconfigurations**, slower incident triage, and reliance on over-privileged access. This erodes **confidentiality** and **integrity** by letting exposure persist unnoticed.

message: AWS Support Access policy is not attached to any role.
status_detail: AWS Support Access policy is not attached to any role.

analytic.name: At least one IAM role has the AWSSupportAccess managed policy attached

finding_info.desc: Presence of an **IAM role** that has the AWS managed `AWSSupportAccess` policy attached, designating a support role for interacting with **AWS Support Center** and related tooling.
finding_info.title: At least one IAM role has the AWSSupportAccess managed policy attached
types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Create a dedicated IAM role for AWS Support with `AWSSupportAccess` and:
- Restrict who can assume it; require MFA and time-bound access
- Enforce **least privilege** and **separation of duties**
- Monitor usage via audit logs and review assignments regularly

risk_details:
Without a dedicated support role:
- Case creation and escalation can be delayed, prolonging outages (**availability**)
- Teams may use admin/root, increasing blast radius (**confidentiality/integrity**)
- Audit trails of support actions are weaker, hindering investigations

message: Block Public Access is not configured for the account 123456789012.
status_detail: Block Public Access is not configured for the account 123456789012.

analytic.name: S3 account-level Block Public Access ignores public ACLs and restricts public buckets

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3** account-level **Block Public Access** is assessed for `ignore_public_acls` and `restrict_public_buckets` to confirm centralized blocking of ACL-based public access and limiting buckets with public policies to in-account principals.
finding_info.title: S3 account-level Block Public Access ignores public ACLs and restricts public buckets
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Turn on account-level **Block Public Access** (prefer enabling all four: `block_public_acls`, `ignore_public_acls`, `block_public_policy`, `restrict_public_buckets`) to enforce least privilege. For legitimate access, use private buckets with **CloudFront**, VPC endpoints, or presigned URLs. Regularly review policies with IAM Access Analyzer.

risk_details:
Absent these settings, **public ACLs** and broad bucket policies may grant internet or cross-account access. This risks:
- Confidentiality: bulk data exfiltration
- Integrity: object overwrite/tampering
- Availability: malicious deletions or malware hosting, triggering takedowns

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have correct cross region replication configuration.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have correct cross region replication configuration.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has cross-region replication configured to a bucket in a different region

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon S3 buckets** use **cross-Region replication** with `versioning` and an enabled rule that targets a destination bucket in a different AWS Region.

Buckets with same-Region targets, missing destinations, or disabled `versioning` don't meet this replication posture.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has cross-region replication configured to a bucket in a different region
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Enable **CRR** to a different Region with `versioning` and least-privilege roles.

- Replicate needed prefixes and metadata
- Consider `S3 Replication Time Control` for tighter RPO
- Protect deletes via `delete marker` strategy and Object Lock
- Monitor replication metrics and test DR regularly

Align with **defense in depth** and availability by design.

risk_details:
**Single-Region storage** creates an availability gap: a Regional outage, control-plane isolation, or denial of service can make data **unreachable**.

Lack of replication raises RPO/RTO, delaying recovery and disrupting multi-Region workloads. Missing replicas also weaken data **integrity** during restore from corruption or deletion.

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have event notifications enabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have event notifications enabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has event notifications enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** define a **notification configuration** that publishes bucket events (for example `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, `s3:ObjectRemoved:*`) to a destination. The evaluation identifies buckets that lack any notification setup.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has event notifications enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/NIST 800-53 Controls

remediation.desc:
Enable **S3 event notifications** for relevant events (e.g., `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, `s3:ObjectRemoved:*`) and route to controlled destinations (SNS, SQS, Lambda, EventBridge).

Use prefix/suffix filters, avoid recursive triggers, and enforce **least privilege** on targets. Pair with object-level logging for **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Missing notifications leaves object and bucket changes **unseen**, weakening **integrity** and **availability** oversight. Undetected deletions, policy drift, or replication issues can stall data pipelines (S3 to Lambda/SQS), slow incident response, and allow tampering or exfiltration to persist longer.

message: Server Side Encryption is not configured with kms for S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012.
status_detail: Server Side Encryption is not configured with kms for S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has server-side encryption with AWS KMS

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** use server-side encryption with **AWS KMS** keys, including dual-layer `aws:kms:dsse`. The evaluation identifies buckets whose default encryption is `aws:kms` or `aws:kms:dsse` rather than SSE-S3.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has server-side encryption with AWS KMS
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable default **SSE-KMS** (or **DSSE-KMS** for highly sensitive data). Use a customer-managed key, enforce **least privilege** and separation of duties for key usage, and require KMS encryption via bucket policy (specify `aws:kms` and a designated key). Monitor key activity in **CloudTrail** and consider **S3 Bucket Keys** to control cost.

risk_details: Without **KMS-based encryption**, data relies only on SSE-S3, reducing **confidentiality** controls. Missing key policies and grants weakens **least privilege**, cross-account scoping, and the ability to disable or rotate keys. Lack of **KMS audit trails** obscures key usage, hindering detection of misuse and **defense in depth**.

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have a lifecycle configuration enabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have a lifecycle configuration enabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has a lifecycle configuration enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** use **Lifecycle configurations** with at least one rule `Status: Enabled` to automate object `Transitions` and `Expiration` based on age, prefix, or tags
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has a lifecycle configuration enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Define **Lifecycle policies** by data classification: set `Expiration` to enforce retention, use `Transitions` to lower-cost classes, and enable `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload`. For critical logs, keep versioning and, *if required*, **Object Lock**. Limit who can change lifecycle using least privilege and separation of duties.

risk_details: Without lifecycle rules, objects persist indefinitely, driving costs and retaining sensitive data beyond policy. Unchecked log/version growth strains operations and recovery. Long-lived data increases exposure if the account is compromised and can break required deletion timelines, affecting confidentiality and availability.

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has MFA Delete disabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has MFA Delete disabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has MFA Delete enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** are assessed for **MFA Delete** status. MFA Delete requires a second factor to permanently delete object versions or change `Versioning` configuration. The finding highlights buckets where this protection is not enabled.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has MFA Delete enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc: Enable **MFA Delete** on sensitive, versioned buckets so permanent deletions and `Versioning` changes require a second factor. Apply **least privilege** to restrict version purge actions, enforce **change control**, and combine with **Object Lock** or immutable backups for defense in depth.

risk_details:
Without **MFA Delete**, a compromised or over-privileged identity can irrevocably purge object history or change versioning.

This erases recovery points, degrading data **availability**, weakening **integrity**, and increasing the blast radius of account compromise or ransomware.

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has Object Lock disabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has Object Lock disabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has Object Lock enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** have **Object Lock** enabled at the bucket level, applying WORM controls to object versions
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has Object Lock enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Enable **Object Lock** for critical data and set appropriate default retention in `GOVERNANCE` or `COMPLIANCE` mode.

Apply **immutability** and **least privilege** by restricting permissions that bypass retention, and use legal holds when you need indefinite protection for investigations or regulatory requirements.

risk_details:
Without **Object Lock**, object versions can be deleted or overwritten, undermining data **integrity** and **availability**.

Threats include ransomware erasing backups, insider or mistaken deletions, and tampering that defeats recovery. Inability to enforce retention or legal holds increases exposure to data loss and compliance gaps.

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has versioning disabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has versioning disabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has object versioning enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for **object versioning** being `Enabled`, which maintains multiple versions of the same object key for historical state retention
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has object versioning enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Enable **S3 versioning** for buckets holding important or shared data.
- Enforce **least privilege** to limit delete/overwrite
- Use **Object Lock** and/or **MFA Delete** for stronger protection
- Apply **lifecycle rules** to manage noncurrent versions and costs
- Layer with backups/replication for **defense in depth**

risk_details:
Without **versioning**, deletions and overwrites remove the only copy, undermining **availability** and **integrity**.
- Compromised identities or buggy apps can mass-delete/corrupt data
- No historical versions means limited rollback and irrecoverable loss

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have a bucket policy, thus it allows HTTP requests.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 does not have a bucket policy, thus it allows HTTP requests.

analytic.name: S3 bucket policy denies requests over insecure transport

finding_info.desc:
**Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for a bucket policy that enforces **secure transport** by denying requests when `aws:SecureTransport` is `false`.

Buckets without this explicit denial, or without a policy, are treated as allowing access over insecure transport.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket policy denies requests over insecure transport
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices/Network Reachability
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc:
Enforce **HTTPS-only** access with a bucket policy that denies requests when `aws:SecureTransport=false`.

Prefer **private access** (VPC endpoints or CloudFront with TLS), avoid S3 website endpoints, apply **least privilege**, use short-lived HTTPS **pre-signed URLs**, and monitor logs for insecure access attempts.

risk_details: HTTP access exposes object data and auth details to **eavesdropping** and **man-in-the-middle** attacks. Captured **pre-signed URLs** can be replayed to exfiltrate data. Traffic can be intercepted or altered, undermining **confidentiality** and **integrity** of S3 content.

message: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has server access logging disabled.
status_detail: S3 Bucket datalake-raw-123456789012 has server access logging disabled.

analytic.name: S3 bucket has server access logging enabled

finding_info.desc: **Amazon S3 buckets** are evaluated for **server access logging** configured to record access requests and deliver logs to a designated destination bucket.
finding_info.title: S3 bucket has server access logging enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark

remediation.desc: Enable **server access logging** and send logs to a dedicated log bucket with least privilege, retention, and monitoring. Complement with **CloudTrail data events** for object-level visibility. Apply **defense in depth** by centralizing logs and protecting them from tampering.

risk_details: Without access logs, object reads, writes, and deletions may go untracked, hindering detection of unauthorized access and data exfiltration. This degrades forensic visibility, delays incident response, and weakens evidence integrity, impacting confidentiality and integrity.
